ai.title: File request prompts enforce project root paths
ai.summary: System and file-request prompts now explicitly require full paths from the project root, correcting relative import ambiguity. This change targets `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to ensure consistent file resolution. The updated instructions direct the agent to normalize relative subdirectory imports into absolute root-relative paths during request generation.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to look at a file, it will now always use the complete path starting from the main project folder, even if the file is normally referenced by a shorter, relative path in the code. This prevents confusion about which file is being requested, so you get the correct file every time instead of a wrong or missing one. This rule is already in effect.

ai.title: Disable Helicone LLM security for OpenAI prompts
ai.summary: The Helicone-LLM-Security-Enabled header is commented out in backend/src/openai-api.ts, disabling Helicone's LLM security layer for OpenAI prompt requests. This change alters how prompt safety checks are handled for OpenAI API calls routed through Helicone. The modification is scoped to the OpenAI API client configuration.

eli5.text: Requests sent to the AI assistant through the OpenAI connection no longer run through Helicone's built-in safety filter before reaching the model. If you looked at the logs today, you'd see that the security header that used to be attached to every OpenAI call is now turned off, meaning prompts are passed through without that extra layer of automated checking for harmful content.

ai.title: Pin dependency versions to exact releases
ai.summary: Dependency ranges converted from caret (^) to exact versions across backend, npm-app, and root package.json files. Includes major upgrades for @anthropic-ai/sdk (0.24.3 to 0.26.1), axios (0.24.0 to 1.7.4), and typescript (5.3.2 to 5.5.4), alongside minor/patch bumps for express, zod, ws, and others. Ensures reproducible builds by eliminating floating version resolution.

eli5.text: The app now locks in exact versions of its supporting software libraries instead of allowing flexible ranges, so every build uses the same tested versions and is less likely to break unexpectedly. This affects the backend server, the internal tooling app, and the root project configuration. If you looked, you'd see dependency version numbers pinned to specific releases rather than ranges, and TypeScript and several libraries like Axios and the AI SDK were bumped to newer major versions.

ai.title: Backend Dockerfile switches to Bun runtime
ai.summary: backend/Dockerfile uses oven/bun:1 with multi-stage build. deploy.sh copies common/src to backend/src/common before docker build. tsconfig.json paths updated to resolve common/* from ./src/common/*.

eli5.text: You won't directly notice this change unless you peek at the server setup behind the scenes. The team swapped out the old runtime system that powers their backend service to a newer, faster one called Bun, which replaces the previous Node-based setup. This required some behind-the-scenes adjustments to how files are shared between parts of the codebase and how those paths are looked up. The change is internal and already live, affecting only how the backend runs in containers.

ai.title: Dockerfile env copy and npm version check fix
ai.summary: Dockerfile release stage copies .env. WebSocket checkNpmVersion reads package.json only in production, preventing path errors in dev. CLI key handler adds detectPasting call. Affects backend/Dockerfile, backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts, npm-app/src/cli.ts.

eli5.text: The app now keeps a copy of its environment settings file inside each production deployment, so servers have the configuration they need without manual setup. When the app checks whether the installed version matches the latest release, it only looks up that information while running in production, skipping the lookup during local development to avoid errors. The command-line interface now also recognizes when a user is pasting text, improving reliability of the input experience. These fixes are live today for anyone running the latest production deployment.
